audit.why: 50.25% over 1622 games is a coin-flip lane, and the shape the entry gives it is right: Vladimir wins the poke phase because Malphite's armour is worthless against pure AP, Level 6 is Malphite's single kill window, and the two-item stage is Vladimir's on scaling. The chart giving him five stages with two 'Skill' is a fair reading of an even matchup. The only mismatch is whys[2], which says 'it's even' under a stage the chart awards to Vladimir.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1], mid, wants.you[1] and whys[4] all hang the entire matchup on flanking 'while Sanguine Pool is on cooldown', and never once give the number.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and only reaches 16s at rank 5, which makes it one of the longest untargetability cooldowns in the game and turns the entry's vague instruction into a countable window. Against Unstoppable Force at 130s that ratio is brutal at rank 1 and merciful later, and the player needs to know which. It also matters that the pool grants two full seconds of untargetability, not an instant dodge — R thrown at a Vladimir who has already pooled is gone for the whole duration.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and 16s at rank 5, and gives two seconds of untargetability. Count it before every R — that number is the whole matchup.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood is called 'E pool of blood', 'E's delayed blood-pool burst' and 'E (the blood-pool burst)' in four places, borrowing the pool imagery from Sanguine Pool, which is W.
audit.why: Beyond the name confusion, the conflation buries the single best piece of counterplay in the matchup. Riot's text for Tides of Blood: Vladimir 'pays his own health to charge up a reservoir of blood which, when released, deals damage in the area around him but can be blocked by enemy units'. It is blockable by minions. A Malphite who keeps the wave between himself and a charging Vladimir eats none of it — and it costs Vladimir health to cast, which is why his poke is not free. None of that is on the page.
audit.corrected: Tides of Blood (E) is a charged AoE around Vladimir that costs him his own health and is BLOCKED BY ENEMY UNITS — stand behind your minions and it does not reach you. Sanguine Pool (W) is the untargetability.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (E Tides of Blood, cd 13/11/9/7/5, range 600; W Sanguine Pool)

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere in either layer, and Hemoplague is never named or described.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags this pairing for needs-antiheal off Transfusion and Hemoplague, and both are load-bearing. Transfusion is a free-cast heal on 9s falling to 4.6s that is massively empowered when his resource bar is full — that is the sustain the entry keeps calling 'Q drain' without ever naming the answer to it. Hemoplague makes affected enemies take increased damage for its duration and then heals him for each champion it hit, which turns a teamfight Malphite engage into his heal. Grievous Wounds is the item and it appears nowhere.
audit.corrected: Transfusion is a no-cost heal on 9s down to 4.6s, empowered at full resource. Hemoplague amplifies the damage you take and then heals him per champion hit. Grievous Wounds is core, not optional.
sources: champ-data/_kits/vladimir.json (Q Transfusion cd 9/7.9/6.8/5.7/4.6; R Hemoplague cd 120, heal)

audit.whatIsWrong: Crimson Pact is never mentioned, and the entry twice treats Vladimir as a burst mage who 'one-shots a low-economy tank'.
audit.why: Crimson Pact converts bonus health into AP and AP into bonus health, so a scaled Vladimir is not a squishy who dies to one knock-up — he is a durable AP threat, and the health items that would normally make him killable make him stronger. That reframes the level-6 plan: Unstoppable Force onto Vladimir is a set-up for your team, not an execution, and holding it for his carry is usually better.
audit.corrected: Crimson Pact turns his bonus health into AP and his AP back into health, so he is durable as he scales — your R on him sets up a kill, it does not land one.

audit.why: The itemisation call is right and both layers agree on it, which is rare in this file: Vladimir's damage is entirely magic, so Malphite's armour defends nothing and MR is the buy. Worth preserving. Armour remains worth some investment because Ground Slam's damage is calculated from it, but as an offensive stat only, and the entry never claims otherwise.

edits.before: Vlad owns the opening — your armor from W and E means nothing against his pure AP, so all your defensive stacking just doesn't matter here. He drains you with Q and zones you off the wave with E's delayed blood-pool burst while you have no trade button before W and E are online. Don't walk up to last-hit into a charged E; take CS with the tip of Q from max range and accept you're giving up the pre-6 window to a champion you can't punish.
edits.after: Vlad owns the opening — his kit is entirely magic, so the armour Thunderclap and Ground Slam give you defends nothing. But Tides of Blood (E) is answerable: he charges it, it costs him his own health, and it is blocked by enemy units, so keeping minions between you takes the poke off the table. Transfusion (Q) is the free heal on 9s at rank 1 that undoes your chip. Take CS with the tip of Seismic Shard and concede the pre-6 window to a champion you cannot punish yet.

edits.before: At 4-5 you stabilize — Granite Shield refreshes when you back off and W's armor lets you farm through his poke, but you still can't kill him on the ground. Level 6 is your whole lane: Unstoppable Force is your one moment of real threat, so flank him with R the instant Sanguine Pool is on cooldown, knock him up and chain Q's slow to finish before he can untarget. If his pool is up, do NOT throw R into it — you'll waste your only window and feed his scaling.
edits.after: At 4-5 you stabilise — Granite Shield refreshes when you break off and Thunderclap's armour holds the wave, but you still cannot kill him on the ground. Level 6 is your whole lane, and it is one number: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and gives two full seconds of untargetability. Count it. Flank with R the moment it is spent, knock him up, and chain Seismic Shard's move-speed steal to finish. If the pool is up, do NOT throw R — you lose a 130s ultimate to a two-second dodge.

edits.before: This is Vlad's game, not yours. Full-AP Vlad pools your R the moment you dash, kites your Q slow with Rylai-into-his-own movement, and his empowered Q+E burst ignores every point of armor you've stacked. Your value flips entirely to engaging onto his carries for your team and peeling — accept you lose the straight 1v1 and play Malphite as the R-flank frontline, never as a duelist who can kill a fed drain-mage.
edits.after: This is Vlad’s game. Crimson Pact turns bonus health into AP and AP back into health, so he is not a squishy your knock-up deletes — he is durable, and his burst ignores every point of armour you own. Buy MR, and buy Grievous Wounds: Transfusion is a free heal on 4.6s at rank 5, and Hemoplague amplifies your incoming damage then heals him per champion caught. Play the R-flank frontline, never the duelist.

notes: No packet defects flagged for this matchup and the itemisation call was already right — both layers correctly say his damage is pure magic and armour defends nothing, which I left intact. Three additions instead. (1) The best piece of counterplay in the matchup was missing: Tides of Blood is charged, costs Vladimir his own health, and is BLOCKED BY ENEMY UNITS, so standing behind your minions takes his poke off the table entirely. The entry called it 'E pool of blood' and 'E's delayed blood-pool burst' in four places, borrowing Sanguine Pool's imagery and hiding the interaction. (2) Four strings said to flank 'while Sanguine Pool is on cooldown' and never gave the number. It is 28s at rank 1 falling to 16s, with two full seconds of untargetability — that number is the entire level-6 plan against a 130s ultimate. (3) No anti-heal anywhere in either layer, in a matchup _missing-interactions.json flags for it: Transfusion is a no-cost heal on 9s down to 4.6s and Hemoplague heals him per champion hit while amplifying the damage you take. Also added Crimson Pact, which was absent — it converts bonus health into AP and back, so the entry's picture of a squishy who gets deleted by one knock-up is wrong, and R on him is a set-up rather than an execution. CHART: left alone. Five Vladimir stages with two Skill is a fair shape for a 50.25% lane; the only mismatch is whys[2] saying 'it's even' under a Vladimir stage, and I rewrote that string so it no longer claims parity.
